overall_summary: Deduplicating 47 unique Shorts reveals a clear bifurcation in channel performance: first-person hypothetical space simulations ('What If You Fell Into...') and extreme exoplanet anomalies drive the highest reach (800-1,050+ views) and top engagement (up to 3.7% like ratio), whereas redundant psychology trivia and re-uploaded basic science facts severely stall (<50 views). The sweet spot for retention and algorithmic push sits consistently at 19-21 seconds with visceral, sensory stakes.

winning_patterns.pattern: First-Person Hazard Scenarios ('What If You Fell Into...')
winning_patterns.evidence: Recent videos exploring extreme planetary hazards ('What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet' - 1,029 views, 38 likes; 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice' - 972 views; 'What If You Fell Into the Darkest Planet' - 823 views) consistently triple channel average views.
winning_patterns.action: Anchor hooks around visceral, immediate second-person stakes ('What happens if you step onto...') paired with extreme cosmological environments.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet Darker Than Coal' (1,029 views, 36 likes) and 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (981 views, 21 likes) generated the strongest baseline velocity among informational Shorts.
winning_patterns.action: Feature single mind-bending astrophysical paradoxes with punchy visual comparisons rather than generic trivia.

weak_patterns.pattern: Recycled Psychology and Brain Fact Clichés
weak_patterns.evidence: Multiple iterations of 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' flatlined between 5 and 53 views; 'The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head' stalled at 17 views.
weak_patterns.action: Immediately retire overused psychological trivia and generic brain facts.

weak_patterns.evidence: Identical titles uploaded repeatedly (e.g., 'Why Space Is Completely Silent' across 4 distinct IDs, 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' across 3 IDs) cannibalized traffic down to 34 and 10 views.
weak_patterns.action: Never re-upload identical titles/concepts; enforce strict uniqueness checks across all batches.
